section_summary: This section combines three 1940 military-attaché biographies of senior Japanese Army officers with correspondence concerning the illness of Privy Councillor Count Kentaro Kaneko. Most of the section documents American diplomatic responses to the deaths and state funerals of Prince Kinmochi Saionji and Fleet Admiral Marquis Heihachiro Togo, including disputes over the designation and publicity of special foreign representatives. The Togo papers also cover American naval participation, Japanese expressions of thanks, and controversy over unsuitable music broadcast by NBC during the funeral observances.

subfiles.title: Military Attaché Report No. 10,144: Major General Issaku Nishihara
subfiles.from: Harry I. T. Creswell, Military Attaché, Tokyo
subfiles.to: U.S. War Department, Military Intelligence Division
subfiles.about: A biographical résumé of Major General Issaku Nishihara and his appointment to inspect supply movements in French Indochina.
subfiles.summary: The report traces Nishihara's education, promotions, staff assignments, disarmament work at Geneva, and wartime service in China. It describes him as familiar with France and well suited to head the delicate inspection mission to French Indochina.

subfiles.title: Charge Slip for Military Intelligence Enclosure
subfiles.about: A file-control slip recording the charge of an enclosure from decimal file 894.44.
subfiles.summary: The page is an administrative charge record rather than substantive correspondence. It identifies the item as an enclosure connected with a Military Intelligence Division report.

subfiles.title: Military Attaché Report No. 10,157: Lieutenant General Hideki Tojo
subfiles.from: Harry I. T. Creswell, Military Attaché, Tokyo
subfiles.to: U.S. War Department, Military Intelligence Division
subfiles.about: A résumé of Hideki Tojo's military career and appointment as War Minister in the second Konoe Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: The report lists Tojo's family background, military education, promotions, commands, and senior posts in the Kwantung Army and War Ministry. It characterizes his appointment as the Army's approved choice and describes him as an able soldier with strong views suited to contemporary conditions.

subfiles.title: Military Attaché Report No. 10,197: Lieutenant General Yoshitsugu Tatekawa
subfiles.from: Harry I. T. Creswell, Military Attaché, Tokyo
subfiles.to: U.S. War Department, Military Intelligence Division
subfiles.about: A career outline and assessment of Lieutenant General Yoshitsugu Tatekawa following his designation as ambassador to Moscow.
subfiles.summary: The report recounts Tatekawa's Russo-Japanese War exploit, military promotions, international-conference service, commands, decorations, and retirement. It presents him as unusually knowledgeable about international affairs and notes his subsequent activity in Kingoro Hashimoto's nationalist Young Men's Party.

subfiles.title: Case Jacket: Count Kentaro Kaneko
subfiles.about: The jacket identifies the case concerning Privy Councillor Count Kentaro Kaneko.
subfiles.summary: The cover records Kaneko's name, Privy Council membership, and the opening date of the correspondence. It contains no substantive narrative beyond filing instructions.

subfiles.title: Mrs. Burnett's Handwritten Note and Enclosures Concerning Count Kaneko
subfiles.about: A partly illegible personal communication forwarding material concerning the ailing Count Kentaro Kaneko and praising his friendship with the United States.
subfiles.summary: Burnett describes Kaneko as an exceptionally devoted lifelong friend of America and forwards an enclosed cable or related material. The badly degraded handwriting also contains personal reflections and an inscription apparently connected with Kaneko.

subfiles.title: Letter from Cordell Hull to Frances H. Cameron Burnett
subfiles.about: Hull thanks Burnett for her note and expresses hope for Count Kaneko's recovery.
subfiles.summary: Hull acknowledges Burnett's February 25 note and its generous personal references. He expresses sorrow over Kaneko's illness, hopes for a complete recovery, and returns her two enclosures.

subfiles.title: Letter from Count Kentaro Kaneko to Cordell Hull
subfiles.about: Kaneko thanks Hull for his good wishes and reports that he is slowly recovering from pneumonia.
subfiles.summary: Kaneko states that Mrs. Burnett forwarded Hull's February 27 letter and that he was pleased by Hull's hope for his recovery. He says his pneumonia was dangerous at his age, that doctors regarded his survival as miraculous, and that illness delayed his reply for three months.

subfiles.title: Letter from Cordell Hull to Count Kentaro Kaneko
subfiles.about: Hull acknowledges Kaneko's report of recovery and offers his best wishes.
subfiles.summary: Hull expresses happiness at receiving Kaneko's May 29 letter. He says he sincerely trusts that Kaneko's recovery from his recent illness is now complete.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on a Proposed Reply to Count Kaneko
subfiles.about: The memorandum recommends acknowledging Kaneko because of his influence and longstanding pro-American position.
subfiles.summary: The division explains that Mrs. Burnett evidently forwarded Hull's February letter to Kaneko. It describes Kaneko as an influential Privy Councillor, Theodore Roosevelt's friend, a participant in American mediation of the Russo-Japanese War, and the leader of Japan's pro-American group.

subfiles.title: Instruction Forwarding Hull's Letter to Count Kaneko
subfiles.about: The Department asks the ambassador to deliver Hull's enclosed letter to Count Kaneko.
subfiles.summary: The instruction encloses a letter from the Secretary of State addressed to Kaneko. The American ambassador is requested to transmit it to the addressee.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1200 on Prince Saionji's State Funeral
subfiles.about: Grew asks whether he may represent the president if other major powers appoint special representatives to Saionji's funeral.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports that Saionji will receive a state funeral on December 5 comparable in importance to Togo's 1934 funeral. He intends to discourage special foreign appointments but requests authority to represent the president if British or French representatives are specially designated.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1193 Announcing Prince Saionji's Death
subfiles.about: The embassy announces the death of Prince Kinmochi Saionji.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports that Prince Saionji, the last surviving genrō, died the previous night. The telegram is a brief death notification without additional analysis.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1207 Reporting Action on Condolences
subfiles.about: Grew confirms that he acted on the Department's instruction concerning Saionji's death.
subfiles.summary: The embassy states that action was taken in accordance with Department telegram No. 496. This records delivery of the American message of sympathy.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 496 Conveying Condolences for Prince Saionji
subfiles.about: Hull directs the embassy to convey American sympathy to Saionji's family and the Japanese government.
subfiles.summary: The message praises Saionji as a distinguished statesman widely known and respected in the United States. The embassy is asked to extend sympathy on behalf of Hull and the American government and to report the action taken.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1243 Transmitting Matsuoka's Thanks
subfiles.about: Grew forwards the Japanese foreign minister's acknowledgment of American condolences.
subfiles.summary: The telegram translates a November 28 note from Yosuke Matsuoka. Matsuoka expresses profound gratitude on behalf of the Imperial Japanese Government for the condolences conveyed by the American Secretary of State and government.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1268 on Grew's Special Designation
subfiles.about: Grew reports that he will attend Saionji's funeral as the president's special representative.
subfiles.summary: After learning that special designations would gratify the Japanese government, Grew notified the Foreign Office that he would attend in that capacity. He adds that the British ambassador would do likewise and that the French ambassador had requested instructions.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1275 on French Representation at Saionji's Funeral
subfiles.about: Grew reports that the French ambassador will also serve as a special representative.
subfiles.summary: Grew supplements his earlier report on the diplomatic arrangements. His French colleague has now received instructions to act as a special representative at Saionji's funeral.

subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note of Thanks for Saionji Funeral Representation
subfiles.from: Morito Morishima, Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim
subfiles.about: Japan thanks the United States for designating Grew to represent the president at Saionji's funeral.
subfiles.summary: Morishima conveys his government's gratitude for Grew's attendance as proxy for the American head of state. He also expresses the sincere thanks of Saionji's bereaved family and asks that the appreciation be passed to the appropriate American authorities.

subfiles.title: Instruction No. 2089 Forwarding the Japanese Note of Thanks
subfiles.about: The Department forwards Morishima's note thanking the United States for Grew's funeral representation.
subfiles.summary: The instruction encloses a copy of the Japanese chargé's December 7 note. It summarizes the gratitude of the Japanese government and Saionji family for Grew's designation as the president's special representative.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of the Japanese Note on Saionji's Funeral
subfiles.from: Sumner Welles, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Department acknowledges Japanese thanks and confirms that they were conveyed to appropriate officials.
subfiles.summary: Welles acknowledges Morishima's December 7 note concerning Grew's attendance at Saionji's funeral. He states that its expression of appreciation has been passed to the appropriate officials of the U.S. government.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1291 Listing Special Representatives at Saionji's Funeral
subfiles.about: Grew reports which countries sent special representatives and notes the lack of press coverage.
subfiles.summary: Special representatives came from the United States, France, Manchukuo, and Great Britain. Grew observes that the Japanese press made no mention of this fact.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Publicity for Saionji's Funeral
subfiles.about: The memorandum summarizes Grew's despatch on the absence of publicity for the special foreign representatives.
subfiles.summary: It records the British ambassador's complaint that failure to publicize his royal designation wasted an opportunity to counter adverse propaganda. Matsuoka attributed the omission to disorganization during the merger of the Foreign Office News Department into the General Information Department.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5205: State Funeral of the Late Prince Saionji
subfiles.about: Grew reports on the Japanese press's failure to identify four ambassadors as special funeral representatives.
subfiles.summary: Grew encloses the British ambassador's account of his complaint to Matsuoka. He adds that Hidenari Terasaki suggested the representatives' special status escaped notice because the four senior ambassadors occupied their normal precedence positions.

subfiles.title: British Ambassador's Minute of Conversation with Matsuoka
subfiles.to: British Embassy record; copy to the American Embassy
subfiles.about: The British ambassador protests the failure to publicize his appointment as the King's special representative.
subfiles.summary: Craigie tells Matsuoka that the lack of publicity squandered a valuable opportunity to counter adverse propaganda. Matsuoka agrees and blames temporary disorganization caused by merging the Foreign Office News Department into the General Information Department.

subfiles.title: Peking Circular on the Death of Prince Saionji
subfiles.from: Nelson Trusler Johnson, circulating a note from Y. Tsuchida
subfiles.about: The circular announces Saionji's death and funeral and states that the American Embassy flag will be flown at half-mast.
subfiles.summary: Tsuchida's enclosed note reports Saionji's death on November 24 and the state funeral scheduled for December 5 in Tokyo. Johnson, as American and senior ambassador, informs his colleagues that the American Embassy will also lower its flag that day.

subfiles.title: Case Jacket: Admiral Marquis Togo
subfiles.about: The jacket identifies the papers concerning special mention of Admiral Marquis Togo.
subfiles.summary: The page serves as the cover for the Togo correspondence. It records the subject, date, and filing classification but contains no substantive report.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 79 Conveying Condolences on Togo's Death
subfiles.to: American Embassy, Tokyo, for the Japanese Minister for Foreign Affairs
subfiles.about: Hull sends American condolences following the death of Admiral Togo.
subfiles.summary: Hull states that the emperor has lost a loyal servant, Japan one of its most illustrious men, and the world an esteemed personality. The embassy is instructed to transmit the message to the Japanese foreign minister.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 103 Confirming Delivery of the Togo Condolence Message
subfiles.about: Grew confirms delivery of Hull's message and reports correction of Togo's title from count to marquis.
subfiles.summary: The condolence message was delivered to the Minister for Foreign Affairs on May 30. Grew changed Togo's title because the rank of marquis had been conferred immediately before his death.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 105 Recommending U.S. Naval Attendance at Togo's Funeral
subfiles.about: Grew recommends sending a U.S. Asiatic Fleet unit to Togo's state funeral.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports planned British, French, and possibly Italian naval representation at the June 5 funeral. He supports the naval attaché's recommendation that a unit of the U.S. Asiatic Fleet also attend.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation with the Japanese Ambassador
subfiles.about: Phillips records Ambassador Saito's delivery of Hirota's reply and comments on Togo and Prince Konoe.
subfiles.summary: Saito reports that Hull's condolence message received prominent and favorable treatment in the Japanese press and summarizes Togo's final years. He also reminds Phillips of Prince Konoe's forthcoming private visit connected with his son's graduation.

subfiles.title: Koki Hirota's Reply to Cordell Hull's Condolences
subfiles.about: Hirota thanks Hull for American sympathy on Togo's death.
subfiles.summary: Hirota expresses deep gratitude for the sentiments conveyed by Hull. He specifically acknowledges the condolences of the American government and people.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 80 on U.S. Naval Representation
subfiles.about: The Department reports Navy approval for Asiatic Fleet representation and requests coordination on foreign attendance.
subfiles.summary: The Navy Department considers it advisable for the commander-in-chief or a suitable representative to attend Togo's funeral. Grew is asked to verify other countries' plans and notify Admiral Upham in Shanghai.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 109 Confirming Admiral Upham's Arrival Plan
subfiles.about: Grew reports that Admiral Upham will arrive aboard the Augusta for Togo's funeral.
subfiles.summary: Upham plans to reach Yokohama at daybreak on June 5 aboard his flagship, the Augusta. Grew has informed the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs of his intended participation.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 111 on French Special Representation
subfiles.about: Grew asks whether he should represent the U.S. president after France designates presidential and governmental representatives.
subfiles.summary: France has designated its ambassador to represent the French president and its Asiatic Fleet commander to represent the government. Grew warns that this may give the French envoy precedence over the American ambassador and requests consideration of a corresponding U.S. designation.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 86 Authorizing Conditional Presidential Representation
subfiles.about: The Department conditionally authorizes Grew to represent the president at Togo's funeral.
subfiles.summary: The Department regards special head-of-state representatives at such funerals as unusual but does not want to offend Japan by lagging behind other powers. Grew is told to consult the British representative and may follow the French precedent, while Upham would represent the U.S. government.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 112 on British and Italian Decisions
subfiles.about: Grew explains when he will use the authority to act as the president's special representative.
subfiles.summary: The British chargé and Italian ambassador have sought instructions but received no replies. Grew says he will accept special status only if Britain appoints a representative, because he wishes to avoid establishing an awkward precedent.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 114 Declining Special Status
subfiles.about: Grew initially decides not to attend Togo's funeral as a special representative.
subfiles.summary: Available information indicated that only the French ambassador had received a special designation. On that basis, Grew reports that he will attend without claiming special representative status.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 115 on Grew's Last-Minute Special Designation
subfiles.about: Grew explains his last-minute decision to represent the U.S. president at Togo's funeral.
subfiles.summary: Although Japanese officials had said special representatives would receive no distinction, the funeral arrangements gave them priority, and Britain notified Grew at the last moment of its royal designation. Grew therefore invoked his authorization, obtained first rank among foreign representatives, and judged the change necessary for American prestige; France, Great Britain, and Manchukuo also had special representatives.

subfiles.title: Department Approval of Grew's Action
subfiles.about: The Department approves Grew's decision and asks about formal confirmation of his designation.
subfiles.summary: The brief telegram approves the ambassador's last-minute action at Togo's funeral. It also asks Grew to determine whether an additional formal presentation or notification is expected.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 117 on Formal Confirmation of Grew's Designation
subfiles.about: Grew reports that a confirming embassy note will satisfy the Japanese Foreign Office.
subfiles.summary: The Foreign Office advises that a note confirming Grew's designation as of June 5 will be sufficient. Grew intends to follow that procedure unless instructed otherwise.

subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note Thanking the U.S. Navy
subfiles.about: Japan expresses appreciation for Admiral Upham's attendance at Togo's state obsequies.
subfiles.summary: Saito reports that Grew informed Tokyo of the U.S. Navy's intention to send Upham to the funeral. Acting under instructions, he asks Hull to transmit the Japanese government's deep appreciation to the Secretary of the Navy.

subfiles.title: Letter Forwarding Japanese Appreciation to the Secretary of the Navy
subfiles.from: R. Walton Moore, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The State Department forwards Saito's note thanking the Navy for Admiral Upham's attendance.
subfiles.summary: Moore encloses a copy of the Japanese ambassador's June 6 communication. The letter calls the Navy's attention to Japan's appreciation of Upham's participation in Togo's obsequies.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Ambassador Saito
subfiles.from: R. Walton Moore, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Department acknowledges Japan's thanks and confirms transmission to the Navy.
subfiles.summary: Moore acknowledges Saito's June 6 note regarding Admiral Upham. He states that the message of appreciation has been conveyed to the Secretary of the Navy.

subfiles.title: Navy Department Acknowledgment of the Togo Correspondence
subfiles.about: The Navy acknowledges the Japanese note and states that the correspondence was forwarded to Admiral Upham.
subfiles.summary: The letter confirms receipt of the State Department's June 12 communication and enclosure. A copy of the exchange has been sent to Admiral Upham.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 821: Condolence Message on Togo's Death
subfiles.about: Grew transmits copies of the formal exchange of condolence notes concerning Togo's death.
subfiles.summary: The despatch encloses Grew's May 30 note delivering Hull's message and Hirota's May 31 reply. Grew records that he delivered the American message personally and that Hirota instructed Ambassador Saito to convey his thanks in Washington.

subfiles.title: Embassy Note No. 243 Delivering Hull's Condolences
subfiles.about: Grew formally communicates Hull's condolence message on the death of Admiral Togo.
subfiles.summary: The note reproduces Hull's tribute to Togo as a loyal servant, illustrious Japanese, and internationally respected figure. Grew delivers the message to Hirota in his official capacity as Minister for Foreign Affairs.

subfiles.title: Foreign Office Note No. 56/P Replying to the Togo Condolences
subfiles.about: Hirota acknowledges Hull's message and expresses gratitude for American sympathy.
subfiles.summary: Hirota thanks Hull for the condolences sent in connection with Togo's death. He reports that he has also conveyed his appreciation through Ambassador Saito in Washington.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 822: Grew's Designation at Togo's Funeral
subfiles.about: Grew transmits the formal notes concerning his appointment as presidential representative at Togo's funeral.
subfiles.summary: The despatch reviews the telegrams that led to Grew's special designation for the June 5 ceremony. It encloses his notification to Hirota and the Foreign Office reply conveying the Japanese government's thanks to the president.

subfiles.title: Embassy Note No. 246 Confirming Grew's Special Designation
subfiles.about: Grew formally notifies Hirota that he will represent the U.S. president at Togo's funeral.
subfiles.summary: Grew states that he has been designated under instructions from his government. He confirms that he will attend the June 5 ceremony as the president's special representative.

subfiles.title: Foreign Office Note No. 60/P Acknowledging Grew's Designation
subfiles.about: Hirota acknowledges Grew's designation and conveys Japanese appreciation.
subfiles.summary: Hirota expresses appreciation for the U.S. president's consideration in appointing Grew. He has instructed Ambassador Saito to transmit the Japanese government's sincere thanks to the president.

subfiles.title: Internal Note on Advising Broadcasters in Future
subfiles.about: The note recommends offering informal advice to broadcasters on future sensitive occasions.
subfiles.summary: The writer sees no need to send the despatch to NBC because the company already has the relevant information. Berkeley of NBC and Butcher of C.B.C. may be told that the Department would informally offer advice in future without accepting responsibility.

subfiles.title: Internal Memorandum on NBC's Funeral Broadcast Error
subfiles.about: The memorandum comments on NBC's broadcast of frivolous music during Togo's funeral observances.
subfiles.summary: The writer says the Department was not consulted and therefore bears no responsibility for NBC's selection. The most surprising aspect is said to be the Japanese broadcaster's failure to turn off the unsuitable music.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 836: NBC Error at Togo's Funeral
subfiles.about: Grew reports Japanese displeasure over NBC's broadcast of inappropriate music following a funeral tribute to Togo.
subfiles.summary: NBC unwittingly included the Yamada Suite, containing music such as “Kappore” normally associated with drinking parties, after Admiral Standley's speech. Japanese opinion recognized NBC's ignorance but blamed the Tokyo office of the Japan Broadcasting Company for failing to stop the program; Grew encloses a press item and exchanged telegrams.

subfiles.title: Pacific Information Article: “Frivolous Melodies by N.B.C.”
subfiles.about: The article reports Japanese anger at frivolous music broadcast during national mourning for Togo.
subfiles.summary: The article says songs including “Echigo-Jishi,” “Kappore,” and “Umegaye” shocked listeners after Admiral Standley's tribute. Captain Taketomi, Lieutenant-Colonel Mikuni, and Keikichi Tanomogi chiefly blame JOAK for failing to interrupt the transmission.

subfiles.title: John F. Royal's Telegram to the Japanese Broadcasting Company
subfiles.from: John F. Royal, National Broadcasting Company
subfiles.about: Royal requests details of the reported misunderstanding over NBC's Togo memorial broadcast.
subfiles.summary: Royal says NBC intended to pay the highest tribute to Togo and cannot understand reports of a problem in Tokyo. He asks what happened and stresses that the company would not knowingly interfere with its commemorative purpose.

subfiles.title: JOAK Reply to John F. Royal
subfiles.to: John F. Royal, National Broadcasting Company
subfiles.about: JOAK explains why the Yamada Suite was inappropriate for the state-funeral broadcast.
subfiles.summary: JOAK attaches no blame to NBC and accepts that the program was selected unknowingly. It explains that the “Kappore” passage resembled festive jazz or dance music and reports that the Japanese press and public were blaming the Tokyo staff.

subfiles.title: Peking Circular on Togo's Death and Funeral
subfiles.from: Senior Minister in Peking, enclosing K. Wakasugi's note
subfiles.about: The circular announces Togo's death and the lowering of Japanese and Spanish flags for his funeral.
subfiles.summary: Wakasugi's enclosed letter reports Togo's death on May 30 and the state funeral in Tokyo on June 5. The senior minister states that the Spanish Legation will also fly its flag at half-mast for the occasion.

subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 125 Thanking the President
subfiles.about: Japan thanks the U.S. president for Grew's attendance as his representative at Togo's funeral.
subfiles.summary: Saito acts on telegraphic instructions from his government. He asks Hull to convey Japan's sincere thanks for Grew's presence at the June 5 funeral as the president's representative.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Japanese Thanks for Grew's Attendance
subfiles.from: William Phillips, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Department confirms that Japan's appreciation has been reported to the president.
subfiles.summary: Phillips acknowledges Saito's June 19 note. He states that the president has been informed of the Japanese government's appreciation for Grew's representation at Togo's funeral.

subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet on Admiral Upham's Interrupted Nanking Visit
subfiles.about: The sheet points to a report on orders directing Admiral Upham from Nanking to Togo's funeral.
subfiles.summary: The referenced document concerns Upham's receipt of orders while visiting Nanking to attend Togo's funeral. His departure interrupted plans made for his entertainment there.

subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet to Grew's Report on the Togo Funeral and Broadcast
subfiles.about: The sheet points to Grew's report on American funeral participation and the broadcasting faux pas.
subfiles.summary: The reference identifies a July 2 report from Grew under another file classification. Its subjects are U.S. participation in Togo's funeral and Japanese annoyance over the NBC or Japan Broadcasting Company error.

subfiles.title: Extract on U.S. Participation in Togo's Funeral and the NBC Incident
subfiles.about: The extract summarizes foreign representation at Togo's funeral and Japanese reaction to the broadcast music.
subfiles.summary: It records Admiral Upham's arrival aboard the Augusta, Grew's presidential representation, and the attendance of foreign naval and diplomatic representatives. It then explains that Japanese criticism of NBC's frivolous music was tempered by recognition that the mistake arose from ignorance, while possible official action appears to have been dropped.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 389 Transmitting the British Admiralty's Togo Memorial Message
subfiles.about: Grew transmits a British Admiralty message for the dedication of a shrine to Admiral Togo.
subfiles.summary: The First Lord of the Admiralty associates the Admiralty and Royal Navy with the Japanese Navy's tribute to Togo. The message praises Togo as a great and gallant sailor and recalls his early British connections with pride.
